5186: 
5187: Bluetooth devices operate in the unlicensed 2.4 GHz Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) band. In many cases, a combination of FDD and TDD techniques are required to achieve acceptable levels of performance.

5285: ##### 7.2. Adaptive Frequency Hopping
5286: 
5287: Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH) allows Bluetooth devices to improve their immunity to interference from and avoid causing interference to other devices in the 2.4 GHz ISM band. The basic principle is that Bluetooth channels are classified into two categories, used and unused, where used channels are part of the hopping sequence and unused channels are replaced in the hopping sequence by used channels in a pseudo-random way. This classification mechanism allows for the Bluetooth device to use either all or fewer than the channels available. The minimum number of channels allowed by the Bluetooth specification is 20 on BR/EDR and 2 on LE.
5288: 
5289: The specification defines the aspects of AFH necessary to ensure interoperability, including the hopping kernel, Baseband behavior, Link Manager Protocol (LMP) commands, Link Layer behavior and commands, and Host Controller interface (HCI) commands and events required to change and configure hopping sequences. The Bluetooth Specification also defines a mechanism that allows for a Peripheral to report channel classification information to the Central.
5290: 
5291: Adaptive Frequency Hopping makes use of metrics obtained through many sources. These metrics are analyzed and then the resulting Channel\_Map is used by the adaptive frequency hopping kernel. The metrics may come from over-the-air measurements, data supplied by the Host (e.g., via HCI commands), or reports by the Peripheral or from other hardware coexistence interfaces.
5292: 
5293: While AFH is a critical element in coexistence, it is not enough in some circumstances.
5294: 
5295: ##### 7.3. Coexistence between Bluetooth Devices and Wireless LAN Devices
5296: 
5297: Coexistence between Bluetooth and Wireless LAN has traditionally been a combination of Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH) and proprietary techniques to prioritize traffic between the two protocols. The specification does not specify signaling between the Bluetooth Controller and a Wireless LAN device.
5298: 
5299: ##### 7.4. Mobile Wireless Standards (MWS) coexistence
5300: 
5301: Significant interference can be present between the Bluetooth radio and a collocated MWS radio operating in frequency bands adjacent to the 2.4 GHz ISM band. This interference can prevent one radio from receiving while the other radio is transmitting.
5302: 
5303: The “Filter recommendations for Coexistence with LTE and WiMAX” whitepaper[\[1\]](#ftn.id263488) describes filter specifications that, in some cases, can reduce collocated interference to an acceptable level. The specification includes complementary solutions to traditional filtering including features for Bluetooth Controllers and Hosts as well as signaling and messaging mechanisms between collocated MWS and Bluetooth radios. [Figure 7.1](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4568344809153633541999654098 "Figure 7.1: MWS coexistence architecture") illustrates the general architecture model for these mechanisms. This architecture assumes separate antennae with limited isolation.
5304: 
5305: ![MWS coexistence architecture](../image/img-b6255c84f9a09cee87d80c77838c44df.png)
5306: 
5307: Figure 7.1: MWS coexistence architecture
5308: 
5309:   
5310:   
5311: 
5312: Two types of solutions have been considered. In the first solution, both Bluetooth transmissions (TX) and receptions (RX) are constrained by collocated MWS activities. Solutions of this type are called Pure TDM (Time Division Multiplexed) Mode. In the second solution, only Bluetooth receptions are affected by collocated MWS transmissions and Bluetooth transmissions do not impact the operation of the collocated MWS. Solutions of this type are called Hybrid Mode and are achieved, for example, by using steep roll-off Band Select Filters (BSFs) for the ISM band in the Bluetooth transceiver. Hybrid Mode applies where the Bluetooth transmission’s effect on MWS is sufficiently reduced via filtering that the Bluetooth device can transmit during the MWS downlink time. This requires a frequency guard band between the Bluetooth and MWS operational frequency ranges as well as constraints on both the Bluetooth BSF and the MWS BSF. The requirement for a time domain solution still remains, but only to protect Bluetooth reception.
5313: 
5314: These solutions are facilitated by an MWS coexistence signaling mechanism (see [\[Vol 7\] Part A](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/mws-coexistence-logical-signaling-specification.html "Part A MWS Coexistence Logical Signaling Specification")) and multiple transport layers (see [\[Vol 7\] Part B](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/wireless-coexistence-interface-1--wci-1--transport-specification.html "Part B Wireless Coexistence Interface 1 (WCI-1) Transport Specification") and [\[Vol 7\] Part C](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/wireless-coexistence-interface-2--wci-2--transport-specification.html "Part C Wireless Coexistence Interface 2 (WCI-2) Transport Specification")).
5315: 
5316: MWS technologies operate in licensed bands and use centralized scheduling to support Wide Area Network services. An MWS radio synchronizes both time and frequency with a network Base Station. The Base Station determines which MWS radio will transmit or receive and when. MWS radios have no control over when to transmit or receive. When Bluetooth transmissions interfere with MWS receptions in the MRT, the MWS radio can be rendered unusable if the Bluetooth radio transmits freely. [Figure 7.2](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4592183766329633675245948569 "Figure 7.2: MWS receptions interfered with by uncontrolled Bluetooth transmissions") shows how Bluetooth activity can interfere with every MWS reception opportunity and similarly how MWS transmissions can interfere with Bluetooth reception. In the example shown in [Figure 7.2](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4592183766329633675245948569 "Figure 7.2: MWS receptions interfered with by uncontrolled Bluetooth transmissions") the Bluetooth device in the MRT is operating as the Central of a piconet. Blocks marked with a “C” are single slot Central transmissions and those marked with a “P” are single slot Peripheral transmissions. The times at which reception by the MWS device may be corrupted by Bluetooth transmissions are marked with a red shade.

5319: 
5320: Figure 7.2: MWS receptions interfered with by uncontrolled Bluetooth transmissions

The Bluetooth radio only gets one transmission/reception opportunity every MWS frame, as shown in [Figure 7.3](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4594931415764833542004009049 "Figure 7.3: Bluetooth radio has reduced transmission/receiving opportunities").
5326:

5328:

5334: Consequently, three out of four (for 5 ms MWS frames) or seven out of eight (for 10 ms MWS frames) slot pairs of Bluetooth can be punctured by MWS activities. Furthermore, since Bluetooth inquiry and paging use a sequence of 16 channels at a time, when the Bluetooth radio in the MRT is performing inquiry or paging the channel sequence will repeat every 5 ms resulting in the same channels being repeatedly punctured by the collocated MWS activities, see [Figure 7.4](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4496827204268833542005725801 "Figure 7.4: Bluetooth radio can suffer inquiry/page failures"). 5356: ##### 7.5. Synchronizing Bluetooth with an external timing source
5357: 
5358: This section provides an example to illustrate the synchronization of the Bluetooth CLK with an MWS system so that the Bluetooth slots line up with the Downlink and Uplink times of the MWS system. The external frame in this example is LTE TDD Frame Configuration #1 and special subframe configuration #1; however the same mechanisms can be used for any external TDD/TDMA protocol. The example shows a time span of 10 ms.
5359: 
5360: [\[Vol 7\] Part A](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/mws-coexistence-logical-signaling-specification.html "Part A MWS Coexistence Logical Signaling Specification") defines the timing of the MWS frame as a fixed offset from the FRAME\_SYNC signal in the coexistence signaling. This is shown in [Figure 7.6](architecture.html#UUID-910bcc24-8e30-7032-63b0-b99b82636bce_figure-idm4642746399540833542009166284 "Figure 7.6: Alignment of MWS frame timing and Bluetooth clock") as FS. FS can be defined by the Host as any specific offset within the MWS frame. For a piconet Central, the most useful position for FS is the boundary between the uplink and the following downlink. This is because the Central needs to transmit in a Central slot during the uplink and then receive in the following Peripheral slot during the downlink. Putting FS at this boundary allows the Central to easily align its Bluetooth clock to put it between these slots. The situation is reversed in a Peripheral: FS is most useful on the boundary between the downlink and the following uplink.
5361: 
5362: The HCI command HCI\_Set\_External\_Frame\_Configuration ([\[Vol 4\] Part E, Section 7.3.81](../host-controller-interface/host-controller-interface-functional-specification.html#UUID-a9f595e2-4302-c318-d2a6-34bd9e408ff6 "7.3.81 Set External Frame Configuration command")) can be used to describe the MWS frame timing. This knowledge, together with FS, allows the Bluetooth Controller to align the Bluetooth clock with the MWS frame timing so as to minimize the effect of mutual interference. This is illustrated in [Figure 7.6](architecture.html#UUID-910bcc24-8e30-7032-63b0-b99b82636bce_figure-idm4642746399540833542009166284 "Figure 7.6: Alignment of MWS frame timing and Bluetooth clock"). The red ovals show slot pairs where both MWS and Bluetooth transmit and receive simultaneously and so do not interfere with each other. The MWS frame structure includes a downlink portion (“D”), an uplink portion (“U”), and a special portion (“S”) that includes a downlink and uplink portion separated by a guard period (“GP”).
5363: 
5364: ![Alignment of MWS frame timing and Bluetooth clock](../image/img-9f1f3cc26c818be96e0e2dba9dd2f58c.png)
5365: 
5366: Figure 7.6: Alignment of MWS frame timing and Bluetooth clock

5373: Note: In LTE, if the implementation does not have access to the exact LTE timing it can assume that the downlink-to-uplink boundary is the middle of the GP in a special LTE subframe.
5374: 
5375: ##### 7.6. Piconet clock adjustment
5376: 
5377: As discussed in the previous section, aligning the MWS and Bluetooth clocks correctly greatly improves throughput on both technologies. The Central has two mechanisms at its disposal to mitigate misalignments.
5378: 
5379: Coarse Clock Adjustments can be used to move the Bluetooth CLK using the LMP\_CLK\_ADJ PDU. The clk\_adj\_us parameter is used to align the slots with the MWS alignment point indicated by the FRAME\_SYNC signal. The clk\_adj\_slots parameter can be used to move the CLK several slots forward in time. This can be useful to align e.g. eSCO. Coarse Clock Adjustment is expected to be used only rarely, for instance at MWS connection or when the MWS frame timing changes due to roaming. Coarse Clock Adjustment can only be used when all Peripherals in the piconet support it.
5380: 
5381: The other option for the Central is to use Clock Dragging. This is a method of slowly adjusting the phase of the clock backward or forward by making the slots a few µs shorter or longer, respectively, until the desired CLK phase has been achieved. It should be noted that this is a very slow rate of adjustment, as it is designed to allow a legacy device to track the change, and therefore the requirements of [\[Vol 2\] Part B, Section 1.1](../br-edr-controller/baseband-specification.html#UUID-fed63ce1-f360-62a1-468d-fd3392198bf8 "1.1 Bluetooth clock") mean that Clock Dragging must not be done at a faster rate than the maximum natural drift between devices. For this reason its main use is to facilitate small corrections over time if a misalignment with the MWS system is detected. If any device is connected that does not support Coarse Clock Adjustment, slowly moving the Peripheral using Clock Dragging is the only option.
5382: 
5383: It is recommended to let the collocated device be the Central, when possible, as it can react much faster to correct misalignments. If a Peripheral is the collocated device, doing a role switch to make it Central may be worth considering. Alternatively a Peripheral can send a Piconet Clock Adjustment Request LMP packet to the Central. The Central then has the option to perform a Coarse Clock Adjustment, Clock Dragging, or to reject the request.
5384: 
5385: ##### 7.7. Slot Availability Mask (SAM)
5386: 
5387: Slot Availability Mask (SAM) allows two Bluetooth devices to indicate to each other time slots that are available for transmission and reception. The SAM slot map specifies the availability or otherwise of Bluetooth slots. A slot could be unavailable because of external conditions (e.g., MWS coexistence) or internal conditions (e.g., scatternet commitments). SAM does not impose new mandatory rules for the scheduling of BR/EDR time slots. Instead, it merely provides information which allows Controllers to refine their scheduling of Bluetooth slots to improve performance.
5388: 
5389: SAM slot maps are calculated by the Controller itself based on its scheduling requirements. There are no HCI commands defined specifically for SAM, merely LMP sequences that enable devices to exchange maps and indicate the map in use. The HCI commands HCI\_Set\_External\_Frame\_Configuration (see [\[Vol 4\] Part E, Section 7.3.81](../host-controller-interface/host-controller-interface-functional-specification.html#UUID-a9f595e2-4302-c318-d2a6-34bd9e408ff6 "7.3.81 Set External Frame Configuration command")) and HCI\_Set\_MWS\_PATTERN\_Configuration (see [\[Vol 4\] Part E, Section 7.3.85](../host-controller-interface/host-controller-interface-functional-specification.html#UUID-604c2f69-2470-3a07-4f27-693210b2ba1d "7.3.85 Set MWS_PATTERN Configuration command")) and real-time signals (e.g., MWS\_PATTERN\_Index or FRAME\_SYNC) provided by the Coexistence Logical Interface (see [\[Vol 7\] Part A](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/mws-coexistence-logical-signaling-specification.html "Part A MWS Coexistence Logical Signaling Specification")) contain information concerning the appropriate SAM\_Index and SAM anchor point to use for MWS coexistence; these may therefore trigger these LMP sequences.
5390: 
5391: A Controller may choose to perform a Piconet Clock Adjustment before initiating an LMP\_SAM\_SWITCH sequence so as to increase the number of slot pairs available per MWS frame.

#### 7. 共存与共置

蓝牙设备运行在免许可的 2.4 GHz 工业、科学和医疗（ISM）频段。许多其他技术也使用 ISM 频段，包括无线局域网、无绳电话和微波炉。ISM 频段还与其他频段足够接近，使得蓝牙设备可能成为其他技术的干扰源或受害方。

无线电设备可以是共置的或非共置的。"共置"一词是一个较为宽泛的概念——在本规范中，假设共置的无线电设备位于同一产品（多无线电终端或 MRT）中，并且可能具有协调其活动以减轻干扰的机制。

确定无线电设备之间预期的隔离度对于选择合适的共存机制非常重要。在隔离度充足时，频分双工（FDD）技术效率最高。在隔离度不足或共享天线时，需要使用时分双工（TDD）技术。在许多情况下，需要组合使用 FDD 和 TDD 技术才能达到可接受的性能水平。

本规范支持多种有助于减轻对其他设备的干扰以及将来自其他设备的干扰降至最低的特性。广义上，这些解决方案的类型可分为以下几类：

类型

通过调度或优先级排序，一次仅允许一个无线电设备发射或接收

时间对齐

将共置无线电设备的活动在时域上对齐，通过避免冲突活动来优化性能。例如，多个无线电设备可以同时发射，多个接收可以同时进行，但不能同时发射和接收

频分与时分混合

##### 7.2. 自适应跳频（AFH）

自适应跳频（AFH）允许蓝牙设备提高其对 2.4 GHz ISM 频段中来自其他设备干扰的免疫力，并避免对其他设备造成干扰。其基本原理是将蓝牙信道划分为两类：使用和未使用，其中使用的信道是跳频序列的一部分，而未使用的信道以伪随机方式被使用的信道在跳频序列中替换。这种分类机制允许蓝牙设备使用全部或少于可用的信道。蓝牙规范允许的最小信道数在 BR/EDR 上为 20，在 LE 上为 2。

本规范定义了确保互操作性所需的 AFH 各方面内容，包括跳频内核、基带行为、链路管理协议（LMP）命令、链路层行为和命令，以及更改和配置跳频序列所需的主机控制器接口（HCI）命令和事件。蓝牙规范还定义了一种机制，允许外围设备（Peripheral）向中心设备（Central）报告信道分类信息。

自适应跳频利用从多种来源获得的度量指标。对这些度量指标进行分析，然后将得到的 Channel\_Map 用于自适应跳频内核。这些度量指标可能来自空中测量、由主机提供的数据（例如通过 HCI 命令），或来自外围设备的报告，或来自其他硬件共存接口。

虽然 AFH 是共存中的关键要素，但在某些情况下还不够。

##### 7.3. 蓝牙设备与无线局域网设备之间的共存

蓝牙与无线局域网（WLAN）之间的共存传统上是自适应跳频（AFH）与用于在两种协议之间对流量进行优先级排序的专有技术的组合。本规范不规定蓝牙控制器与无线局域网设备之间的信令。

##### 7.4. 移动无线标准（MWS）共存

蓝牙无线电设备与运行在 2.4 GHz ISM 频段相邻频段的共置 MWS 无线电设备之间可能存在显著干扰。这种干扰可能在一个无线电设备发射时阻止另一个无线电设备接收。

"Filter recommendations for Coexistence with LTE and WiMAX"白皮书[\[1\]](#ftn.id263488)描述了滤波器规格，在某些情况下可将共置干扰降低到可接受的水平。本规范包含对传统滤波的补充解决方案，包括用于蓝牙控制器和主机的特性，以及共置 MWS 与蓝牙无线电设备之间的信令和消息传递机制。[图 7.1](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4568344809153633541999654098 "图 7.1：MWS 共存架构")说明了这些机制的总体架构模型。该架构假设使用具有有限隔离的独立天线。

![MWS coexistence architecture](../image/img-b6255c84f9a09cee87d80c77838c44df.png)

图 7.1：MWS 共存架构

已经考虑了两种类型的解决方案。在第一种解决方案中，蓝牙的发射（TX）和接收（RX）都受到共置 MWS 活动的约束。这种类型的解决方案称为纯 TDM（时分复用）模式。在第二种解决方案中，只有蓝牙接收受到共置 MWS 发射的影响，而蓝牙发射不影响共置 MWS 的运行。这种类型的解决方案称为混合模式，例如可以通过在蓝牙收发器中对 ISM 频段使用陡峭滚降的带选滤波器（BSF）来实现。混合模式适用于蓝牙发射对 MWS 的影响通过滤波充分降低，使得蓝牙设备可以在 MWS 下行时间内发射的情况。这需要在蓝牙和 MWS 工作频率范围之间设置频率保护带，并对蓝牙 BSF 和 MWS BSF 都施加约束。仍然需要时域解决方案，但仅用于保护蓝牙接收。

这些解决方案由 MWS 共存信令机制（见[\[Vol 7\] Part A](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/mws-coexistence-logical-signaling-specification.html "Part A MWS 共存逻辑信令规范")）和多个传输层（见[\[Vol 7\] Part B](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/wireless-coexistence-interface-1--wci-1--transport-specification.html "Part B 无线共存接口 1（WCI-1）传输规范")和[\[Vol 7\] Part C](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/wireless-coexistence-interface-2--wci-2--transport-specification.html "Part C 无线共存接口 2（WCI-2）传输规范")）来支持。

MWS 技术运行在许可频段，并使用集中式调度来支持广域网服务。MWS 无线电设备在时间和频率上与网络基站同步。基站决定哪个 MWS 无线电设备何时发射或接收。MWS 无线电设备无法控制何时发射或接收。当蓝牙发射干扰 MRT 中的 MWS 接收时，如果蓝牙无线电设备自由发射，MWS 无线电设备可能变得不可用。[图 7.2](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4592183766329633675245948569 "图 7.2：MWS 接收受到不受控蓝牙发射的干扰")显示了蓝牙活动如何干扰每个 MWS 接收机会，以及类似地 MWS 发射如何干扰蓝牙接收。在[图 7.2](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4592183766329633675245948569 "图 7.2：MWS 接收受到不受控蓝牙发射的干扰")所示的示例中，MRT 中的蓝牙设备作为微微网的中心设备（Central）运行。标记为"C"的块是单时隙中心设备发射，标记为"P"的块是单时隙外围设备发射。MWS 设备接收可能被蓝牙发射破坏的时间用红色阴影标记。

![MWS receptions interfered with by uncontrolled Bluetooth transmissions](../image/img-c00c88259b1e958fe772a2a20cf6590d.png)

图 7.2：MWS 接收受到不受控蓝牙发射的干扰

即使在最佳相对定时关系下（当蓝牙时隙边界与 MWS 帧边界对齐时），由于与共置 MWS 无线电设备的时分复用，MRT 中的蓝牙无线电设备的发射和接收机会也会减少。蓝牙无线电设备每个 MWS 帧仅获得一次发射/接收机会，如[图 7.3](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4594931415764833542004009049 "图 7.3：蓝牙无线电设备的发射/接收机会减少")所示。

![Bluetooth radio has reduced transmission/receiving opportunities](../image/img-2d5a2aa73855b48f66fb2d70d4675704.png)

图 7.3：蓝牙无线电设备的发射/接收机会减少

因此，对于 5 ms 的 MWS 帧，四分之三的蓝牙时隙对可能被 MWS 活动打断；对于 10 ms 的 MWS 帧，八分之七的蓝牙时隙对可能被 MWS 活动打断。此外，由于蓝牙查询和寻呼一次使用 16 个信道的序列，当 MRT 中的蓝牙无线电设备执行查询或寻呼时，信道序列将每 5 ms 重复一次，导致相同的信道被共置 MWS 活动反复打断，见[图 7.4](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4496827204268833542005725801 "图 7.4：蓝牙无线电设备可能发生查询/寻呼失败")。因此，远程扫描设备很可能无法在当前超时时间内接收到寻呼或查询 ID。

当查询或寻呼信道序列被反复打断时，可以使用 Train Nudging 为时钟位添加额外的偏移，以移动信道序列。

![Bluetooth radio can suffer inquiry/page failures](../image/img-d34f5f6050ed3b6ba627f65a904a4836.png)

图 7.4：蓝牙无线电设备可能发生查询/寻呼失败

由于 MWS 发射干扰 MRT 中的蓝牙接收，执行扫描的 MRT 中的蓝牙无线电设备将无法接收到来自远程查询/寻呼设备发射的高达 50% 的 ID，如[图 7.5](architecture.html#UUID-5f016d95-49d8-dbdc-2188-3ca3a2b150f6_figure-idm4553492656803233542007215495 "图 7.5：蓝牙无线电设备可能发生查询扫描/寻呼扫描失败")所示。

基于不可用于扫描的时隙模式，可以使用广义交织扫描在背靠背扫描期间调整第二次扫描的相位。

![Bluetooth radio can suffer inquiry scan/page scan failures](../image/img-74c1cb520a84a0f18145c6b1aebeed95.png)

图 7.5：蓝牙无线电设备可能发生查询扫描/寻呼扫描失败

##### 7.5. 蓝牙与外部定时源的同步

本节提供了一个示例，以说明蓝牙 CLK 与 MWS 系统的同步，使得蓝牙时隙与 MWS 系统的下行链路和上行链路时间对齐。本示例中的外部帧是 LTE TDD 帧配置 #1 和特殊子帧配置 #1；然而，相同的机制可用于任何外部 TDD/TDMA 协议。该示例显示的时间跨度为 10 ms。

[\[Vol 7\] Part A](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/mws-coexistence-logical-signaling-specification.html "Part A MWS 共存逻辑信令规范")将 MWS 帧的定时定义为共存信令中 FRAME\_SYNC 信号的固定偏移。这在[图 7.6](architecture.html#UUID-910bcc24-8e30-7032-63b0-b99b82636bce_figure-idm4642746399540833542009166284 "图 7.6：MWS 帧定时与蓝牙时钟的对齐")中表示为 FS。FS 可由主机定义为 MWS 帧内的任何特定偏移。对于微微网中心设备（Central），FS 最有用的位置是上行链路与随后的下行链路之间的边界。这是因为中心设备需要在上行链路期间的中心设备时隙中发射，然后在随后的下行链路期间的外围设备时隙中接收。将 FS 放在此边界处使中心设备能够轻松地对其齐蓝牙时钟，使其位于这些时隙之间。在外围设备（Peripheral）中情况相反：FS 在下行链路与随后的上行链路之间的边界处最有用。

HCI 命令 HCI\_Set\_External\_Frame\_Configuration（[\[Vol 4\] Part E, Section 7.3.81](../host-controller-interface/host-controller-interface-functional-specification.html#UUID-a9f595e2-4302-c318-d2a6-34bd9e408ff6 "7.3.81 Set External Frame Configuration 命令")）可用于描述 MWS 帧定时。该知识结合 FS，使蓝牙控制器能够将蓝牙时钟与 MWS 帧定对齐，从而将相互干扰的影响降至最低。这在[图 7.6](architecture.html#UUID-910bcc24-8e30-7032-63b0-b99b82636bce_figure-idm4642746399540833542009166284 "图 7.6：MWS 帧定时与蓝牙时钟的对齐")中进行了说明。红色椭圆表示 MWS 和蓝牙同时发射和接收的时隙对，因此彼此不干扰。MWS 帧结构包括下行链路部分（"D"）、上行链路部分（"U"）和特殊部分（"S"），特殊部分包括由保护期（"GP"）分隔的下行链路和上行链路部分。

![Alignment of MWS frame timing and Bluetooth clock](../image/img-9f1f3cc26c818be96e0e2dba9dd2f58c.png)

图 7.6：MWS 帧定时与蓝牙时钟的对齐

### 注

注：在 LTE 中，如果实现无法获得精确的 LTE 定时，可以假设下行链路到上行链路的边界是特殊 LTE 子帧中 GP 的中间位置。

##### 7.6. 微微网时钟调整

如前一节所述，正确对齐 MWS 和蓝牙时钟可极大提高两种技术的吞吐量。中心设备有两种机制可用于缓解不对齐问题。

粗时钟调整可用于使用 LMP\_CLK\_ADJ PDU 来移动蓝牙 CLK。clk\_adj\_us 参数用于将时隙与 FRAME\_SYNC 信号指示的 MWS 对齐点对齐。clk\_adj\_slots 参数可用于将 CLK 在时间上向前移动若干时隙。这对于对齐例如 eSCO 很有用。粗时钟调整预计仅会很少使用，例如在 MWS 连接时或当 MWS 帧定时由于漫游而改变时。粗时钟调整只能在微微网中所有外围设备都支持时使用。

中心设备的另一个选项是使用时钟拖曳（Clock Dragging）。这是一种通过使时隙分别缩短或延长几微秒来缓慢向前或向后调整时钟相位的方法，直到达到所需的 CLK 相位。应当注意，这是一种非常缓慢的调整速率，因为它旨在允许传统设备跟踪变化，因此[\[Vol 2\] Part B, Section 1.1](../br-edr-controller/baseband-specification.html#UUID-fed63ce1-f360-62a1-468d-fd3392198bf8 "1.1 蓝牙时钟")的要求意味着时钟拖曳的速率不得快于设备之间的最大自然漂移。因此，它的主要用途是在检测到与 MWS 系统不对齐时随时间进行小的校正。如果连接的任何设备不支持粗时钟调整，则使用时钟拖曳缓慢移动外围设备是唯一的选择。

建议在可能时让共置设备作为中心设备，因为它可以更快地对不对齐进行纠正。如果外围设备是共置设备，则可以考虑进行角色切换使其成为中心设备。或者，外围设备可以向中心设备发送微微网时钟调整请求 LMP 分组。然后中心设备可以选择执行粗时钟调整、时钟拖曳，或者拒绝该请求。

##### 7.7. 时隙可用性掩码（SAM）

时隙可用性掩码（SAM）允许两个蓝牙设备相互指示可用于发射和接收的时隙。SAM 时隙映射指定蓝牙时隙的可用性或其他状态。某个时隙可能由于外部条件（例如 MWS 共存）或内部条件（例如散射网承诺）而不可用。SAM 不对 BR/EDR 时隙的调度施加新的强制性规则。相反，它仅提供信息，使控制器能够优化其蓝牙时隙调度以提高性能。

SAM 时隙映射由控制器自身基于其调度需求计算。没有专门为 SAM 定义的 HCI 命令，仅有使设备能够交换映射并指示正在使用的映射的 LMP 序列。HCI 命令 HCI\_Set\_External\_Frame\_Configuration（见[\[Vol 4\] Part E, Section 7.3.81](../host-controller-interface/host-controller-interface-functional-specification.html#UUID-a9f595e2-4302-c318-d2a6-34bd9e408ff6 "7.3.81 Set External Frame Configuration 命令")）和 HCI\_Set\_MWS\_PATTERN\_Configuration（见[\[Vol 4\] Part E, Section 7.3.85](../host-controller-interface/host-controller-interface-functional-specification.html#UUID-604c2f69-2470-3a07-4f27-693210b2ba1d "7.3.85 Set MWS_PATTERN Configuration 命令")）以及由共存逻辑接口（见[\[Vol 7\] Part A](../wireless-coexistence-signaling-and-interfaces/mws-coexistence-logical-signaling-specification.html "Part A MWS 共存逻辑信令规范")）提供的实时信号（例如 MWS\_PATTERN\_Index 或 FRAME\_SYNC）包含有关用于 MWS 共存的适当 SAM\_Index 和 SAM 锚点的信息；因此这些可能会触发这些 LMP 序列。

控制器可以选择在发起 LMP\_SAM\_SWITCH 序列之前执行微微网时钟调整，以增加每个 MWS 帧可用的时隙对数量。
